Maria (support): FYI: customer on PRO reports streaming chat responses stop mid-sentence only when they connect via SSE from their backend. WebSocket path appears unaffected. Happens ~40% of attempts. They provided two server request IDs: req_20260317_abc123 and req_20260317_def456. Posting their minimal curl + server log excerpts below.

Ian (eng-runtime): Can you paste the full server-side log lines for those request IDs (including trace_id/x-request-id headers)? Also which client stack are they using (node fetch, server-side curl, proxy in front)? @Tess can you triage if any recent edge/proxy changes? :eyes:

Maria (support): From customer logs (redacted keys):
```
[2026-03-17T15:12:03Z] INFO req=req_20260317_abc123 trace=trace-7f4a conn=10.1.5.12 method=POST path=/v1/streams status=200 msg="stream open, sending chunks"
[2026-03-17T15:12:13Z] INFO req=req_20260317_abc123 msg="stream closed by client: read ECONNRESET"
[2026-03-17T15:12:13Z] DEBUG req=req_20260317_abc123 headers={"transfer-encoding":"chunked","content-type":"text/event-stream","connection":"keep-alive","x-request-id":"req_20260317_abc123"}
```

They tried a curl like this (customer):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-chat-mini' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Ian (eng-runtime): Thanks. The ECONNRESET on the server side implies the client closed the socket. Could be client buffer flush behavior or an intermediary (NGINX, CF) closing idle connections. Two quick repro asks we should give the customer: 1) reproduce with `curl -N`/`--no-buffer` and `--http1.1`; 2) collect a packet capture or server-side proxy access logs around those req ids.

Tess (oncall): Nginx/proxy misconfigs often cause chunk coalescing/buffering. Ask them to run these local checks: 
- Run curl with no buffering and force HTTP/1.1: `curl -v -N --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" ...`
- If they're behind a load balancer (ALB/NGINX/Traefik), check `proxy_buffering` and `proxy_read_timeout`. For CloudFront/CF, recommend enabling "origin keepalive" and confirm they aren't injecting `Connection: close`.

Ian (eng-runtime): Also request that they capture raw request/response headers from their side. For node-fetch they can do: `fetch(url, { headers, duplex: 'half' })` and log the response headers + `res.body.getReader()` progress. If they can attach a `--trace-ascii` curl log that helps.

Maria (support): I'll send a compact repro guide. Asking customer to run these and paste outputs + upload a debug bundle. Example reproduction steps for them to run locally: 
```
# reproducible curl (no buffering)
curl -v -N --http1.1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-chat-mini' \
  -d '{"input":"stream test"}' --trace-ascii curl_trace.txt
```
Please attach `curl_trace.txt` and the server `x-request-id` values.

Tess (oncall): If they can, ask their infra team to run a short tcpdump on the host that originates the SSE client (10-30s) and share a pcap: `sudo tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.ai and port 443 -w sse_capture.pcap` (they'll need to remove TLS or provide a proxy capture if certs prevent inspection). If they can't share pcap, ask for LB/proxy access logs and `proxy_buffering` settings.

Ian (eng-runtime): One more quick test: have them try connecting through `nghttp` or `h2c` to rule out HTTP/2 middleboxes. And try toggling over websocket path (`/v1/chat/ws`) to confirm it's only SSE. If WS always succeeds and SSE fails, that points to HTTP/1.1 path or proxy behavior.

Maria (support): Customer asked how to produce a debug bundle. I asked them to run our support script (they don't have it). Instead they're going to upload: curl_trace.txt + pprof logs + the two request IDs. I created internal ticket: SUP-4621.

DebugBot: debug bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-support/sup-4621/bundles/1795123456-customer-sse-bundle.tar.gz (linked to SUP-4621). :white_check_mark:

Ian (eng-runtime): I'll pull the bundle and check our edge logs for those x-request-ids. If we see `RST_STREAM` vs client FIN that will tell us who closed first. I'll update SUP-4621 with findings.

Maria (support): Great — customer is running the curl -N test now, will ping back with curl_trace + pcap or logs. Thanks team :pray:
